frontierGarrisons.name: Frontier Garrisons
frontierGarrisons.flavor: A spear at the gate, and the young town sleeps.
frontierGarrisons.text: Garrisoned cities of at most five population gain +2 food.

militaryColonies.name: Military Colonies
militaryColonies.flavor: The drill yard empties into the furrow.
militaryColonies.text: Cities with a Barracks gain +45% production toward settlers and workers.

commonTheEscortedRoads.name: The Escorted Roads
commonTheEscortedRoads.flavor: Where the guard walks, the merchant does not hurry.
commonTheEscortedRoads.text: Routes whose origin has a garrison gain +5 gold. Naval units gain +2 strength while adjacent to one of your traders.

lettersOfMarque.name: Letters of Marque
lettersOfMarque.flavor: A signature turns a pirate into a patriot.
lettersOfMarque.text: Naval combat kills grant 60 gold. Cities with a Harbour gain +38% gold, but produce naval combat units 20% more slowly.
lettersOfMarque.note: The coin is for a kill made by one of your ships, wherever it happens. The extra gold and the slower shipyards both belong to the cities that have a Harbour.

commonRitesOfPassage.name: Rites of Passage
commonRitesOfPassage.flavor: The boy kneels, the soldier stands.
commonRitesOfPassage.text: Gaining a military unit grants 12 faith.

theSacredHost.name: The Sacred Host
theSacredHost.flavor: An army that prays is an army twice fed.
theSacredHost.text: Military units may be purchased with faith in cities with a Temple at the escalating conversion price. Combat kills grant 15 faith.
theSacredHost.note: A soldier bought with faith costs what it would cost to build, converted at the faith rate.

fieldAcademies.name: Field Academies
fieldAcademies.flavor: Every campaign is a lecture somebody survived.
fieldAcademies.text: Your first combat kill each turn grants 23 science. Cities with a Library produce siege units 38% faster.

theEngineerCorps.name: The Engineer Corps
theEngineerCorps.flavor: The wall falls to arithmetic before it falls to stone.
theEngineerCorps.text: Siege units gain +1 movement. Cities with a Workshop gain +30% production toward siege units and +3 science while at war.

theImperialExaminations.name: The Imperial Examinations
theImperialExaminations.flavor: The sword guards the hall; the hall decides who holds the sword.
theImperialExaminations.text: Garrisoned cities with a Monument gain +3 culture and +1 scholar renown.

examinationsOfState.name: Examinations of State
examinationsOfState.flavor: The realm asks its questions in writing, and keeps the answers.
examinationsOfState.text: Cities with a Monument and a garrison gain +2 science and +2 culture per three citizens. Ungarrisoned cities receive no bonus.

marketGardens.name: Market Gardens
marketGardens.flavor: The cabbage that reaches the road is worth two in the field.
marketGardens.text: Farms beside a road gain +1 gold. Domestic routes grant an additional +1 food to their destination.

theProvincialFair.name: The Provincial Fair
theProvincialFair.flavor: Once a year the province remembers it is one.
theProvincialFair.text: Connected noncapital cities with a Market gain +3 food. Their worked plantations, camps and pastures gain +2 gold.

sacredGroves.name: Sacred Groves
sacredGroves.flavor: Some trees were here before the altar, and knew it.
sacredGroves.text: Worked, unimproved forests gain +1 food and +1 faith.

harvestOfferings.name: Harvest Offerings
harvestOfferings.flavor: The first sheaf is never eaten.
harvestOfferings.text: Farms gain +1 faith in cities following your religion. When those cities grow, they gain 10 production.
deferred: a town of your faith that grows is given a day's labour with it

hydraulicSchools.name: Hydraulic Schools
hydraulicSchools.flavor: Water taught us the level, and the level taught us everything.
hydraulicSchools.text: Cities with an Aqueduct gain +20% production toward science buildings. Those beside a mountain also gain +1 science per three citizens.

theHydraulicCommonwealth.name: The Hydraulic Commonwealth
theHydraulicCommonwealth.flavor: A realm is what its water agrees to.
theHydraulicCommonwealth.text: Aqueducts cost 30% less production. Cities with an Aqueduct gain science equal to 20% of their base food surplus, minimum zero, and +1 production per three citizens.
deferred: a share of the grain a town has left over is gained again as learning
theHydraulicCommonwealth.note: Cut from both its decks. Other cards already pay in towns with an aqueduct, and it had too many parts.

gardenCities.name: Garden Cities
gardenCities.flavor: Plant the square, and the square will plant the town.
gardenCities.text: Cities with a Monument gain +1 culture per three worked wild tiles, at most +3. Cities of at least eight population with an Aqueduct gain +1 happiness.

theSculptedLandscape.name: The Sculpted Landscape
theSculptedLandscape.flavor: The master left, and the valley kept the habit.
theSculptedLandscape.text: Farms beside a great-person improvement gain +2 food and +2 culture. Each farm receives this once regardless of the number of adjacent works.

pilgrimMarkets.name: Pilgrim Markets
pilgrimMarkets.flavor: Every shrine grows a street of stalls.
pilgrimMarkets.text: Routes gain +3 gold and +3 faith if either endpoint contains a Holy Site. This pays once per route even when both endpoints qualify.
pilgrimMarkets.note: The first card to pay a trade route in faith; nothing carried it before this one asked. The test is a disjunction, so one shrine is enough and two are not more — a road with a holy site at each end is paid once, which is the card's second sentence. The site is the prophet's work on the ground, anywhere inside either town's borders, and nobody has to be working the hex.

commonTheTithe.name: The Tithe
commonTheTithe.flavor: A tenth of everything, counted twice.
commonTheTithe.text: Cities with a Temple gain gold equal to 25% of their base faith, and +25% gold.

merchantScholars.name: Merchant Scholars
merchantScholars.flavor: He went for pepper and came back with a grammar.
merchantScholars.text: Foreign routes gain +2 science for each Academy in the origin city.

theExchangeOfDiscoveries.name: The Exchange of Discoveries
theExchangeOfDiscoveries.flavor: Two ports, two answers, and neither one wrong.
theExchangeOfDiscoveries.text: +2 science on mines and quarries on a resource. Additional +2 if the city has a market.
theExchangeOfDiscoveries.note: Both lines land on the same hexes; the second is asked of the town that owns the ground, so a seam whose city has raised its stalls is worth two beakers rather than one.

travellingPlayers.name: Travelling Players
travellingPlayers.flavor: The cart is a stage with wheels on it.
travellingPlayers.text: Foreign routes from a city with a Monument gain +2 culture.

theCosmopolitanCourt.name: The Cosmopolitan Court
theCosmopolitanCourt.flavor: Six languages at one table, and the wine does the translating.
theCosmopolitanCourt.text: Cities with a culture building gain +1 renown per outgoing foreign route, at most +3 per city. Great-person improvements worked by such cities gain +3 gold.
theCosmopolitanCourt.note: A city is counted for the trade routes that set out from it to another empire, and never for more than three. The extra gold wants a citizen standing on the work, as every tile bonus does.

cloisterSchools.name: Cloister Schools
cloisterSchools.flavor: Bread in the morning, letters in the afternoon.
cloisterSchools.text: Cities with both a Temple and a Library gain +5 food and +5 science.

theCloister.name: The Cloister
theCloister.flavor: The walls keep the world out and the argument in.
theCloister.text: Cities with a Temple gain science equal to 30% of their base faith. Their Libraries and Universities each gain +3 food.

sacredCommissions.name: Sacred Commissions
sacredCommissions.flavor: The masons were paid in indulgence and stone.
sacredCommissions.text: Cities with a Holy Site gain +38% production toward wonders. Completing a wonder grants 60 faith.

sacredPatronage.name: Sacred Patronage
sacredPatronage.flavor: Genius is cheap where the faithful are many.
sacredPatronage.text: Faith may purchase great-person drafts at the escalating conversion price. Spending a great person grants 30 faith, at most once per turn.
deferred: spending a great person pays faith, but never more than once in a turn
sacredPatronage.note: Half built and therefore not built: a gift may now be held to once a turn, but the moment the world announces is a great one spending themselves on their boon — so a card written on the spending would pay for one of the ways a person may be spent and stay silent for the others.

illuminatedTreatises.name: Illuminated Treatises
illuminatedTreatises.flavor: Gold leaf on a proof nobody can read yet.
illuminatedTreatises.text: Cities with both a Library and a Monument gain +1 science and +1 culture.

commonTheHouseOfWisdom.name: The House of Wisdom
commonTheHouseOfWisdom.text: Worked Academies gain +3 culture. Cities working an Academy gain +1 renown and +30% production toward wonders. Each city receives the city bonus once.

commonMarcherLords.name: Marcher Lords
commonMarcherLords.flavor: The border is a place, and somebody has to live there.
commonMarcherLords.text: Cities founded within four hexes of a foreign border gain +3 defence and +2 production, and cost one less authority, minimum one.

triumphalArches.name: Triumphal Arches
triumphalArches.flavor: Stone remembers the parade long after the army forgets it.
triumphalArches.text: Capturing a city grants 40 culture and +1 general renown. Cities containing a wonder gain +5 defence.
deferred: taking a town raises the name of a general in particular. A town that holds a wonder can be told from one that does not now, but the renown an occasion pays favours nobody in particular — a deed is not a shelf of buildings, and the draw's bias is a fact about what an empire keeps.

theCrusaderOrders.name: The Crusader Orders
theCrusaderOrders.flavor: They took vows, and then they took the coast.
theCrusaderOrders.text: Military units gain +3 strength in territory not following your religion. Capturing a city presses your religion into it.
theCrusaderOrders.note: Taking a city presses your religion on it once, as a prophet would; whether it converts depends on the faith already there. An empire with no religion presses nothing.

theGrainExchange.name: The Grain Exchange
theGrainExchange.flavor: A full granary is a promise other towns can eat.
theGrainExchange.text: Domestic routes from a city with a Granary give +5 food to their destination. Cities receiving one gain +1 happiness.
theGrainExchange.note: Both halves name the same roads, so the grain and the contentment can never disagree about which towns they mean: a domestic route out of a town with a granary. The contentment is paid once per town however many such carts arrive, and it goes the turn the last of them lapses.

theMonasteryLibraries.name: The Monastery Libraries
theMonasteryLibraries.flavor: Copy it twice: once for God, once for the shelf.
theMonasteryLibraries.text: Monasteries give +3 science. Libraries give +2 faith.
deferred: a house of quiet study teaches as well as prays, and a library prays as well as teaches
theMonasteryLibraries.note: Held whole. One half of this asks for a house the realm no longer raises, so that half can never pay — and a card is never bent to fit the half that can.

theMerchantNavigators.name: The Merchant Navigators
theMerchantNavigators.flavor: The chart was drawn to find a market, and found a world.
theMerchantNavigators.text: Ships gain +1 movement. Routes from a city with a Harbour and a Library gain +5 science.

gardenProvinces.name: Garden Provinces
gardenProvinces.flavor: The road brought the seed, and the square brought the song.
gardenProvinces.text: Connected cities with a Monument gain +3 food and +3 culture.

hearthStores.name: Hearth Stores
hearthStores.flavor: What the hearth keeps, the winter cannot ask for.

commonTools.name: Common Tools
commonTools.flavor: One good adze, borrowed by everybody.
commonTools.text: Your capital gains +1 production toward workers and buildings.
deferred: the hammers are for workers and buildings, and for nothing else

watchmen.name: Watchmen
watchmen.flavor: They know which stones are loose.
watchmen.text: Friendly combat units gain +2 strength when defending in your territory.

restingCamps.name: Resting Camps
restingCamps.flavor: A fire, a pot, and nobody shouting.
restingCamps.text: Friendly units that take no action this turn heal an additional 5 health when otherwise eligible to heal.

localMarkets.name: Local Markets
localMarkets.flavor: Two stalls make a market; three make a rumour.

theVillageScribe.name: The Village Scribe
theVillageScribe.flavor: He writes the letters and reads them back wrong on purpose.

publicGatherings.name: Public Gatherings
publicGatherings.flavor: A crowd is a town finding out what it thinks.

householdAltars.name: Household Altars
householdAltars.flavor: The smallest shrine is the one nobody skips.

commonBoundaryStones.name: Boundary Stones
commonBoundaryStones.flavor: Move one at night and the whole valley knows by noon.
commonBoundaryStones.text: Cities with a Monument expand their borders 20% faster. This does not increase draft culture.

theFrontierMilitia.name: The Frontier Militia
theFrontierMilitia.flavor: Every new wall needs a spear behind it.
theFrontierMilitia.text: Each town you found starts with the best melee unit you can build standing in it.

publicWells.name: Public Wells
publicWells.flavor: Dig deep enough and the dry town forgets it was dry.

civicPeace.name: Civic Peace
civicPeace.flavor: Nothing happened today, and that was the achievement.

roadCrews.name: Road Crews
roadCrews.flavor: They mend the road they are standing on, forever.
roadCrews.text: Workers gain +1 movement when starting their turn on a road you own.
deferred: a worker that wakes on one of your roads travels further that day

roadMaintenance.name: Road Maintenance
roadMaintenance.flavor: A gravel barrow beats a rebuilt bridge.
roadMaintenance.text: Road upkeep is reduced by 20%, saving at most 4 gold per turn.
deferred: the upkeep of your roads is reduced, up to a limit each turn

emergencyStores.name: Emergency Stores
emergencyStores.flavor: Sealed jars, and an argument about when to open them.
emergencyStores.text: Cities of at most four population gain +1 food and +1 production toward buildings.
deferred: the hammers are for buildings, and for nothing else

localClerks.name: Local Clerks
localClerks.flavor: The register is the realm, kept in a smaller hand.

publicHospitals.name: Public Hospitals
publicHospitals.flavor: A ward with windows, which was the whole discovery.
publicHospitals.text: Cities of at least eight population gain +1 happiness.

commonLedgers.name: Common Ledgers
commonLedgers.flavor: Everything counted twice, by two people who dislike each other.
commonLedgers.text: Cities with a Market gain +2 science; cities with a Library gain +2 gold.

cityWatches.name: City Watches
cityWatches.flavor: Half a lantern, all night, on every corner.
cityWatches.text: Your cities gain +4 defence. Garrisoned units heal an additional 5 health when otherwise eligible to heal.
deferred: a soldier standing inside one of your towns mends faster there

theHolyArmy.name: The Holy Army
theHolyArmy.flavor: The relic goes at the head of the column and the column keeps up.
theHolyArmy.text: Worked Holy Sites and citadels that stand beside each other each gain +3 faith and +3 culture.

theBarbarianFrontier.name: The Barbarian Frontier
theBarbarianFrontier.flavor: Where the raiders camped, the farmers follow.
theBarbarianFrontier.text: Clearing a barbarian camp claims the camp's hex and every unowned hex around it for your nearest town within five hexes.

theOriflamme.name: The Oriflamme
theOriflamme.flavor: The banner goes where the priest goes, and the army goes with both.
theOriflamme.text: Military units beside one of your religious units gain +4 strength.

theFloodFestival.name: The Flood Festival
theFloodFestival.flavor: The fields are burned, and the smoke is an offering.
theFloodFestival.text: Each tile your workers turn into burned country grants 8 faith.
theFloodFestival.note: Burned country is laid down one tile at a time by a worker, so the faith is paid tile by tile as each one is burned.

theRoadGarrisons.name: The Road Garrisons
theRoadGarrisons.flavor: A soldier at every gate, and a road home from each.
theRoadGarrisons.text: Garrisoned cities with a road to your capital gain +5 food and +5 defence.

convertItOrTaxIt.name: Convert It or Tax It
convertItOrTaxIt.flavor: Pray as we pray, or pay as we ask.
convertItOrTaxIt.text: Captured cities that do not follow your religion gain +5 gold and +3 faith. Captured cities that follow it cost one less authority, minimum one.

warBonds.name: War Bonds
warBonds.flavor: The treasury is the army that has not yet been hired.
warBonds.text: Military units gain +1 strength for every 150 gold in your treasury, at most +5.

professionalSoldiers.name: Professional Soldiers
professionalSoldiers.flavor: A man paid to fight has practised.
professionalSoldiers.text: Units you purchase gain +3 combat strength.
professionalSoldiers.note: The strength is given when the unit is bought while this card is held, and the unit keeps it for life.

theCharteredCompany.name: The Chartered Company
theCharteredCompany.flavor: A company with a charter, a flag and its own soldiers.
theCharteredCompany.text: Once drafted, unlock the Company Guard, a unique gunpowder-age melee unit that can only be bought with gold, in cities with a Barracks. No chair required.
theCharteredCompany.note: Once the charter is drafted, the Company Guard can be hired from late in the last age of the technology tree.

mercenaryContracts.name: Mercenary Contracts
mercenaryContracts.flavor: The captain signs for fifteen turns, and not one more.
mercenaryContracts.text: Cities with a Barracks may hire the best melee or mounted unit you can build for half its gold price. A hired unit costs no upkeep and leaves after fifteen turns.
deferred: hired soldiers who serve for a set time and then leave
mercenaryContracts.note: Not built yet: a unit that leaves the game on its own after a set time is a new kind of unit, and this card needs one.

theMusterOfTheFields.name: The Muster of the Fields
theMusterOfTheFields.flavor: Put down the sickle and pick up the other thing.
theMusterOfTheFields.text: Cities of at least five citizens may spend one citizen to muster their best legally available melee unit. This shares the city's five-turn levy limit. The unit counts as trained.

carriedOffScholars.name: Carried-Off Scholars
carriedOffScholars.flavor: The conqueror carried the scholars home with the treasure.
carriedOffScholars.text: Capturing a city grants science equal to ten times its population.

theSwordOfState.name: The Sword of State
theSwordOfState.flavor: The sword is carried before the ruler, and a soldier walks behind it.
theSwordOfState.text: On draft: the best melee unit you can build is trained in your capital. It costs no upkeep. Seated, this card does nothing.

copyingTheEnemy.name: Copying the Enemy
copyingTheEnemy.flavor: Every captured weapon is taken apart to see how it was made.
copyingTheEnemy.text: Your first kill each turn of a unit you cannot yet build grants science toward the technology that unlocks it, equal to 10% of that technology's cost.

theNewCode.name: The New Code
theNewCode.flavor: A conquered city is a chance to write the law again.
theNewCode.text: Capturing a city opens a draft at once, at no culture cost. This can happen at most once every ten turns.

lootedArt.name: Looted Art
lootedArt.flavor: The statues march home behind the army.
lootedArt.text: Capturing a city grants 20 renown for each great-person work and wonder inside its borders.

theFarmingGarrisons.name: The Farming Garrisons
theFarmingGarrisons.flavor: The soldier who tills the field defends it best.
theFarmingGarrisons.text: Hexes with a fortified military unit gain +1 food and +1 production. Fortified units gain +2 strength.

booksFromTheShips.name: Books from the Ships
booksFromTheShips.flavor: Alexandria copied every book found on the ships in its harbour.
booksFromTheShips.text: Each foreign trade route you send gains +1 science for each technology the destination's owner knows that you do not, at most +4.

scientificTheAssay.name: The Assay
scientificTheAssay.flavor: Weigh it, burn it, then believe it.
scientificTheAssay.text: Hexes with a strategic resource gain +2 science.

scientificTheSoldierScholars.name: The Soldier-Scholars
scientificTheSoldierScholars.flavor: The garrison keeps the library, and reads it on the long watches.
scientificTheSoldierScholars.text: Your military units in your towns gain +5 strength, and each supplies +2 science.

theMerchantShrines.name: The Merchant Shrines
theMerchantShrines.flavor: Every scale has a god leaning on it.
theMerchantShrines.text: Your capital gains +2 faith. Cities working an improved luxury gain +1 faith, once per city.

theWaqf.name: The Waqf
theWaqf.flavor: Given once, and given for ever.
theWaqf.text: Faith buildings you bought with gold provide +3 faith and +2 culture.

theSilkRoadMonks.name: The Silk Road Monks
theSilkRoadMonks.flavor: They travelled with the silk, and left more than they sold.
theSilkRoadMonks.text: Your trade routes carry 100% more religious pressure. Trade routes you send to a city that follows your religion gain +3 gold and +3 culture.
theSilkRoadMonks.note: The religious pressure a trade route carries is doubled by adding the same amount again.

theBrokersRedraw.name: The Brokers' Redraw
theBrokersRedraw.flavor: Anything can be bought, including another look at the table.
theBrokersRedraw.text: You may reroll a draft with gold instead of faith. All other purchasing is 10% more expensive.
theBrokersRedraw.note: Gold opens the door and pays a premium for it: the price is the faith ladder's own figure, multiplied, so faith stays the cheaper way to ask for a fresh hand and the card is a convenience rather than a replacement. The ladder itself is untouched — a redraw in either bank climbs the same rungs and raises the same count — and a hand whose first asking is free stays free in both. The surcharge on the second line reaches every unit and every building this empire buys, in either bank.

dominionTheStandingArmy.name: The Standing Army
dominionTheStandingArmy.flavor: Not raised for a war. Simply raised.
dominionTheStandingArmy.text: Garrisoned units cost no upkeep. Cities with a Barracks gain +30% production toward military units.

theArtDealers.name: The Art Dealers
theArtDealers.flavor: Every new piece in the collection raises the price of the rest.
theArtDealers.text: Each card you draft grants 15 gold.
theArtDealers.note: A charter you draft counts. Passing a draft does not, and neither does taking a Doctrine.
